Climate forecast issue month
Climate forecast issue date

Sampler diagnostics alone are insufficient: convergence statistics for the agriculture and fiscal posterior samplers passed (no divergences, R-hat near one, adequate effective sample sizes), but convergence only certifies that the sampler explored the posterior; it says nothing about whether the fitted model predicts unseen data. Predictive skill must be demonstrated on genuinely out-of-sample observations.

To claim useful forecasts, one would need genuine out-of-sample scoring evidence such as the conditional Bayesian holdout validation reported for agriculture, where the model is trained on data through an earlier cutoff and scored against later realized outcomes using metrics like RMSE, CRPS and interval coverage. Even this is conditional: realized inputs are supplied rather than forecast, and the latest revised history is used rather than real-time vintages.

The same requirement applies to the fiscal model: a conditional Bayesian holdout with realized inputs provides scored evidence of posterior predictive accuracy, but it is not a validation of the full pipeline that must also forecast ENSO and macro inputs jointly.

Additional evidence beyond diagnostics would include rolling hindcast comparisons against challenger models, but the packet's macro validation uses a ridge challenger on final-vintage data and is explicitly not a direct validation of the Bayesian posterior forecasts, so it cannot by itself establish posterior predictive skill.

Crucially, the existing validation exercises use realized (observed) climate and macro inputs and final revised data. Useful real-world forecasts require the ENSO state itself to be predicted, so one would need scored forecasts generated with forecast ENSO inputs rather than realized ones, plus real-time (unrevised) vintage data, to demonstrate end-to-end skill.

The pipeline itself flags limits that additional evidence would need to overcome: historical validation is conditional, causal identification is not claimed, price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled, and official CPC forecasts are marginal rather than joint. Evidence that forecasts remain calibrated under joint input uncertainty and stated macroeconomic paths would therefore be required before claiming useful out-of-sample forecasts.
Agriculture conditional Bayesian holdout RMSE (realized inputs, latest revised history)
Agriculture conditional Bayesian holdout CRPS
Agriculture conditional Bayesian holdout ninety-percent interval coverage
Fiscal conditional Bayesian holdout RMSE (realized inputs, latest revised history)
Fiscal conditional Bayesian holdout CRPS
Fiscal conditional Bayesian holdout ninety-percent interval coverage

Interpretation: passing sampler diagnostics are a necessary but not sufficient condition. They establish that the posterior was estimated faithfully, not that the model has predictive value. A claim of useful out-of-sample forecasts would additionally require (a) scored predictions on data withheld from fitting, (b) forecasts produced with predicted rather than realized ENSO and macro inputs, (c) real-time data vintages rather than revised series, (d) calibration checks showing stated credible intervals achieve their nominal coverage, and (e) demonstrated skill relative to naive or challenger baselines under the joint input uncertainty the actual pipeline faces. None of these are implied by convergence alone, and the packet's conditional validations address only part of this list.

limitations: The packet provides only conditional holdout validation with realized inputs and latest revised history; no fully end-to-end scored forecasts with predicted ENSO inputs are available.
The macro validation series uses a ridge challenger on final vintages and, per the packet, is not a direct validation of the Bayesian posterior forecasts.
The assessment states historical input provenance is incomplete and is for inspection only; recomputation is not possible.
Causal identification is not claimed for either model, and price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled, so validation metrics speak to conditional association, not causal effect estimates.
The fixed evidence packet is bounded; any additional validation evidence required for the claim of useful out-of-sample forecasts is unavailable here and would need to be generated in future work.

Numeric evidence: I can include validation metrics as numeric claims? Question is about explaining needed evidence — descriptive is fine, but a couple of numeric validation metrics could support. Keep it modest: include agriculture/fiscal Bayesian validation RMSE, CRPS, coverage as numeric claims with one evidence ID each. That adds value. Also macro_validation coverage90 values maybe. Keep a few.

Metadata claims: assessment_date "2026-09-07" (evidence 4f42001c805c4bda23b1893b), forecast_issue "2026-08", forecast_issue_date "2026-08-13".

Compose claims.
